doc.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Row, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Timekeeping, Elvin, Tony Williams and Jo Jones; talk of dogs
summary: Discussion of Lester Young's no-bombs advice, drummers influenced by Elvin and Tony Williams, Jo Jones as the timekeeper, then a brief aside on dogs.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I remember reading a quote from Lester Young, like no bombs just tickety-tickety or something like that.

Yeah. Titty-boom baby, Titty boom. You know? That’s what happened when the drummers, Elvin was there, I was there in 1963 when they recorded “Live at Birdland.” And Elvin influenced a lot of drummers, and then Tony Williams influenced a lot of drummers: Buddy Rich used to say when Tony came on, “Oh yeah, great drummer, flounder, flounder. Lightweight. Flounder.”

But Buddy, he loved Art, he loved Elvin, he used to come by all the time. But you know the main guy with that was Jo Jones. Papa Jo. He was the guy. You see? But it’s timekeeping. I mean that’s the problem I have today. You see? Everybody’s got something to say but there’s no definition to the time. The people who remember used to dance to this.
My dog is keeping time right now.
Oh that’s great. I used to have, I’ve been into breeding them for about thirty years. I went from the whippets and then I had just poodles. I had to just put them to sleep. They had gotten old.
